content.title: About
content.content: Pickled pork pig's feet are a traditional snack made from boiled pig's trotters that are then cured in a brine with vinegar, spices, and aromatic herbs. The feet develop a jelly‑like texture, a rich aroma, and a mildly sour taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The feet are rich in collagen, which turns into a gel during long cooking.
In Russia and Eastern Europe they are often served with beer or as part of a cold appetizer platter.
Classic recipes include mustard seeds, black pepper, bay leaf, and sometimes garlic.
Some regions add apple cider vinegar to the brine for a brighter flavor.
Properly brined feet can keep in the fridge for several weeks.

items.title: High in collagen
items.content: Collagen supports skin, joint, and connective‑tissue health.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Contains calcium, magnesium and phosphorus important for bone health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Pickled foods can contribute to elevated blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Pig meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions.

items.title: Digestive heaviness
items.content: Feet are tough to digest and should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Improper storage may allow pathogenic growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve cold, sliced thinly, often with mustard, rye bread, or sauerkraut. They can be added to salads or enjoyed as a beer snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the refrigerator, submerged in the original brine, in an airtight container. At +4 °C they stay good for 4–6 weeks. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration appears.
